reading: The proposal rewrites one relation, Mill Compact to Keeping the channels (E3, E11). Before, purchased draw owed grain-labour to the rebuild only under Alternative B. After, it owes it in every season, whatever finale is chosen. E1 says nothing else changes and no finale is decided. Read plainly, the Compact's labour duty moves from one unchosen finale option into the baseline world. That sits beside records that still say the Compact's purchased draw carries no return labour (E19, E63), so the proposal may sharpen a tension with those retained statements rather than settle it.

concerns.title: Compact's return duty becomes unconditional
concerns.earlier: Under B, purchased draw owes grain-labour to the rebuild.
concerns.proposed: Purchased draw owes grain-labour to the rebuild in every season.
concerns.reading: The relation keeps its identifier and its target, but its scope widens from a conditional on one finale option to a standing duty. Interpretation: the Compact moves from an outside buyer who draws without labour toward a party with a continuing obligation to the commons. The recorded text does not say what grain-labour does for the spring.
counterevidence: The change is one relation's function text; no node, question or other relation changes (E1).
concerns.competing_reading: The wording change may only generalise a clause already implied in the Compact's settlement, without changing how the Compact is staged.

concerns.title: Compact draws without return labour
concerns.earlier: Purchased shares draw without return labour; the Compact's purchased draw carries no return labour.
concerns.reading: These records remain exactly as before while the changed relation now says purchased draw owes grain-labour every season. They may be read together (no labour at purchase, a later duty) or as a contradiction. The record does not say which the author intends.
counterevidence: E1 asks that every other relation stay as it is, so the retained wording may be a deliberate boundary and not an oversight.
concerns.competing_reading: 'Without return labour' may describe the Book 6 purchase moment, and the new duty a later, separate obligation, so both stand.

concerns.title: Grain-labour as B's distinguishing clause
concerns.earlier: Alternative B lists grain-labour from the Compact as one of its own features.
concerns.reading: If the duty applies in every season, grain-labour is no longer something only B brings. B may then be defined by its binding rota, lot-drawn Table and sunset. The Book 30 phase still says the Compact's settlement is a clause of B or C, which the new relation may leave out of step.
counterevidence: B remains recorded unchanged, so its grain-labour clause is still present (E13).

concerns.title: Alternative A's 'nothing is owed' alongside a Compact duty
concerns.earlier: Under A, draw is decoupled from hands; care is counted and nothing is owed.
concerns.reading: A is not chosen. If A were chosen, a standing Compact duty would be an obligation that A's wording says does not exist. Whether A's 'nothing is owed' covers outside buyers or only the valley's households is not recorded.
concerns.competing_reading: A concerns the valley's mutual dependence; a Compact duty could be treated as a separate trade term outside A's care economy.

concerns.title: What 'the rebuild' means, and from when
concerns.proposed: Duty is owed to the rebuild in every season.
concerns.reading: A new uncertainty. The records mention a Lowfen rebuild by lineage crews in Book 20 and channel labour needed before the Long Return in Book 30. Which rebuild the duty serves, and from which Book it starts, is not stated, and the choice changes what the Compact owes and when.
counterevidence: E31 names return labour and Book 20 lineage crews but does not mention the Compact or grain.

concerns.title: Hands and draw remain the governing variable
concerns.reading: The governing thread, its Book 20 conversion and the Ledger link that sets draw by hands owed are all unchanged. The proposal adds a labour source in kind and does not recast how draw follows hands.

inheritance.text: Book 24 is only listed by title, and its decisions on the examined questions were not read. The records do not show whether it carries any concern about the Compact's labour duty.

The Spring Ledger is a long-form fantasy Series exploring a shared water commons, the institutions that govern it, the meanings attached to obligation, and the consequences of changing collective practices. Its identity should preserve wonder, discovery, everyday belonging, meaningful relationships, institutional transformation, material consequences, and the possibility of hopeful flourishing. Do not turn it into a generic escalating-villain epic.

Experience brief: Wonder, discovery, meaningful adventure, everyday belonging, emotionally consequential relationships and an ultimately hopeful possibility of flourishing. Author-fixed experience brief; working and noncanonical.

1. Reckoned Water: The Ledger governs. Stone Hall credit is proven false from the share-marks, and a lower terrace runs wild; the Hall's monopoly breaks at a local cost. Book 1 reads the measure-marks as evidence and does not read the script. The first partial reading of the script is Book 8. Protagonist's agency comes from evidence and a coalition, not inheritance.

2. The Turn: The Source governs. Open records make shares a commodity. Compact purchases draw water without return labour, so the physical balance is the constraint on what the institutions can do. Maintenance knowledge concentrates in old lineages (Books 9-11). The first partial reading of the script (Book 8) makes the Old Hand contested knowledge.

3. The Old Hand: The Old Hand governs. Legitimacy no longer rests on the Ledger alone. The Unmeasured Return is a costly, physically consequential choice: it stabilises the lower valley and disturbs the high cistern. The stewardship tally records care, not debt, and the counted Turn matches return to draw, which keeps the high terraces from surfeit. The Reading Hall is founded as a public institution with its own readings.

4. Settled Water: Co-governance. Ledger, Source and Old Hand share the field, and no single engine dominates. Both conflicts come from settled practice, not from a new antagonist. Conflict A is unequal capacity to maintain shared channels. It makes hands set part of draw for the first time in the series, and it gives lineage crews a claim on draw. Conflict B is two proven practices, the counted Turn and the gift practice, which contest one outlet. The valley answers with a Gate Table that sets the schedule and holds no record.

5. Unmeasured: The Source is the physical deadline. The Long Return is a deep-store pulse, predicted by the Balance Stones from Book 23. It needs two things Arc IV left the valley: channel labour, which is hands, and a Gate schedule that routes the surge. Books 23-26 carry the Brightwater generation's inheritance. Books 27-29 carry the Compact's bid and, under Alternative C, the ratification window. Book 30 chooses among three mechanisms. proposal.proposed_summary: The Spring Ledger, consolidated working architecture W6, derived from W5 (PR #554, commit d6dd636d). Working and noncanonical; not author-approved. The author-fixed intentions are recorded separately as Studio intentions. The prose architecture is 01-series-architecture.md in the package. The Series keeps five arcs, the three co-governing engines (Ledger, Source, Old Hand), the Arc IV conflicts, Book 23's inheritance and the Book 30 finale. Books 1-15 keep the original's events; Book 1 reads the share-marks as evidence, and the first partial reading of the script is Book 8. The Hollow Gate, the Gate Table, the Special Draw Right and the Book 15 surfeit mechanism are agent-proposed construction additions. Finale Alternatives A, B and C are not chosen, and each states its costs. Not decided: whether shared accounting binds; which finale alternative is preferred; the Compact's settlement; whether the Hollow Gate and Gate Table are accepted; the reform stance; the flood's losses; the Special Draw Right's status. The high cistern's storage is not established, and no value for it is canon. The Harrow Lowe gate is inherited from the original and is recorded as a provisional concept, not in this candidate.

reach_meaning: A later Book may receive the change, but only through the cited inheritance; the inheritance is conditional on the author's decision.
